title: Bose-Einstein Condensates in Time Dependent Traps
abstract: We present analytical results for the macroscopic wave function of a Bose-Einstein condensate in a time dependent harmonic potential. The evolution of the spatial density is a dilatation, characterized by three scaling factors which allow a classical interpretation of the dynamics. This approach is an efficient tool for the analysis of recent experimental results on the expansion and collective excitation of a condensate.
summary: This paper develops an analytical theory to model Bose-Einstein condensates expanding from time-dependent harmonic traps. By using a unitary scaling transform on the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, the complex dynamics are reduced to solving for three key scaling parameters. This method allows researchers to quantitatively analyze experimental measurements of cloud expansion and collective excitations to determine material properties like the scattering length.
main_problem: To derive analytical results for the macroscopic wave function of a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) evolving within a time-dependent harmonic potential.
main_result: The BEC dynamics are entirely characterized by the evolution of three scaling parameters ($\lambda_j(t)$), allowing for *ab initio* calculation of time-of-flight signals and fitting experimental data to determine scattering lengths.
method: The authors employ a unitary quantum scaling transform applied to the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, reducing the complex dynamics to solving coupled differential equations for the scaling factors.
model_or_system: The system is a BEC governed by the time-dependent Gross-Pitaevskii equation in an anisotropic harmonic trap. The initial state uses the Thomas-Fermi approximation, and the evolution is analyzed via classical gas analogies.
key_observables: Spatial density profile, aspect ratio of the cloud width ($W_z/W_\perp$), and scattering length ($a$).
important_parameters: The three scaling factors $\lambda_j(t)$, the trapping frequencies $\omega_j(t)$, and the interaction strength $g$ (related to scattering length $a$).
main_assumptions: Approximations include neglecting terms of order 2 in the modulation parameter ($\epsilon$) and assuming linear response for small excitations. The mean-field treatment is noted to fail for long free oscillation times.
figures_summary: Figure 2 compares theoretical predictions (solid line) with experimental data (diamonds from MIT) showing the aspect ratio versus free oscillation time ($	au_o$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the GPE and introduces the scaling transform. It derives the differential equations for $\lambda_j(t)$, analyzes specific cases like sudden trap opening, and then details the linear response theory to calculate excitations after modulation and time-of-flight.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful analytical framework for analyzing non-equilibrium dynamics in trapped quantum gases, connecting macroscopic observables (like aspect ratio) directly to fundamental interaction parameters ($a$) without needing direct measurement of trap frequencies.
